liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Wipe Out** (2 reviews, 1 other source): The drummers launched it after someone in the audience called for it; it is sometimes labeled Pipeline; A surf groove runs straight into Big Railroad Blues [1][4][11]
- **Jounny B. Goode** (1 review): The reviewer hears more fire and energy than in any version the Dead played on their own [6]
- **Baby What You Want Me to Do** (1 other source): This song is also known as Peepin & Hidin [1]
- **Louie Louie** (1 review): A jam links Louie Louie and Twist and Shout, which the reviewer finds improvisationally excellent [13]
- **David Gans Speaks** (1 review): This is a 32-second bumper announcement by David Gans [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Peggy Sue**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **That;ll Be the Day**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Jounny B. Goode**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Baby What You Want Me to Do**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [14]
- **Wipe Out**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Louie Louie**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 9 archived performances [14]
- **Twist and Shout**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Blue Moon**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Big Railroad Blues [14]

## The recordings

- **gd69-09-07.sbd.dfinney.5808.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 10 songs; 28 min; rated 3.38/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: The soundboard sounds good, with a pleasant, relaxed atmosphere; The recording sounds pretty good [5][7]

## Around the show

- Jefferson Airplane members Jorma, Jack and Joey Covington sat in with the Dead; Covington handled some of the vocals [1]
- Joey Covington, the Airplane's drummer, sings on parts of the show [2]
- Jorma Kaukonen of Jefferson Airplane and Hot Tuna takes part in the loose, garage-style jamming [4]
- Mickey and Bill, the two drummers, stay out of each other's way [5]
- The set feels fast and frantic, like a dance party, with Jorma playing loose and hard [6]
- Jorma is on stage and plays strongly in this garage-band style session [7]
- The drumming on the first couple of tracks is extremely fast, in a loose, drunken jam setting [9]
- The reviewer finds the playing and singing sloppier, possibly from drinking, than anything else on a Dead recording [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-09-07.sbd.dfinney.5808.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Finney; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Dick Latvala is credited with finding this Family Dog jam session tape [2]
